chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id said: Uthman ibn Isa narrated to us from Sama'ah who said:

I asked him about al-ghulul, so he said: 'Al-ghulul is everything that is taken (captured/taken) from the Imam, and eating the wealth of the orphan and its like. And al-suh (illicit gain) is many types, among them the earnings of the cupper, the wage of the prostitute, and the price of wine. As for bribery in judgment, it is disbelief in Allah, Exalted and Mighty.'

key_terms.اَلْغُلُولُ: Ghulul (booty/taken property, specifically from the Imam)

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of ghulul and suh in Shia jurisprudence and what is the ruling on bribery in judgment?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Samaanah elaborates on the concept of *al-ghulul* (plunder or misappropriation) specifically in the context of the Imam, linking it to the consumption of orphans' wealth. He further categorizes *al-suh* (usury or illicit gain) through specific examples like cuppers' earnings and wine sales, culminating in the profound theological assertion that judicial bribery constitutes *kufr* (disbelief) in Allah.
